purpose: Define how carefully selected official-source material may be converted into privacy-minimised test fixtures while preserving provenance, date and legal context.
eligibility: Source must be authoritative for the fact being tested.
Source provenance must be recorded before redaction.
The material must be necessary for the test objective.
Personal data must be minimised or redacted where not necessary.
The fixture must retain enough provenance to distinguish it from synthetic data.
The fixture must not be used to imply live retrieval of the underlying source.

provenance_record.source_reference: Provision, record reference, document identifier or other locator where appropriate.
provenance_record.redaction_summary: What was removed or generalised and why.

redaction_rules: Remove unnecessary names, addresses, folio numbers, account numbers and other identifiers.
Do not alter the substantive fact being tested.
If redaction changes evidential meaning, the fixture must be rejected.
Never fabricate missing text to make a redacted record appear complete.
Keep an internal provenance record even when public/test output is minimised.
guardrails: Source-derived fixture evidence is for controlled testing unless separately promoted through the legal evidence process.
A source-derived fixture does not equal a live retrieval event.
A fixture cannot silently become production evidence.
Historical source material must remain date-aware.
Public display must not expose unnecessary personal data.
If provenance or substantive meaning cannot be preserved, do not create the fixture.
